images.alt: The mouth of the bay at first light: the red and white safe-water mark, and the club’s line of orange buoys behind it
The beginners' course on one waterline: from the slipway, the orange float, the red can, the green cone and the orange buoy line, the water deepening at each, a dashed course joining them
A small orange float with a red pennant, in shallow water off the slipway
The red can, a red buoy fifty metres out
The green cone, a green buoy across the channel
The buoy line: three orange course buoys, a swimmer at the middle one
Two days of tide in the bay: the water rising and falling, slack water marked in red at every turn, and in orange the two swims, at the slack that falls at first light
A flat horizon at first light, the safe-water mark small at its edge
Three swim caps, orange, pink and white, at the waterline
The buoy line across the bay, six orange buoys on one rope
The slipway running into the water, the red can out in the bay
Rock pools at low water, kelp at their edges and a starfish in one
A swimmer’s wake on still water, an orange cap at its point
A red flask and two enamel mugs of tea on a rock after a swim
The jetty in winter, the safe-water mark beyond it
